title: fix(plugin-map): a lookup-typed marker description renders its display name instead of crashing the popup
body:
Fixes #10456
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`ObjectMap` copied the raw `descriptionField` value onto each marker, and three readers treated it as text. The desktop popup and the mobile record sheet put it in JSX, and the search filter called `.toLowerCase()` on it. The map's own object fetch expands every declared relation (`buildExpandFields(objectSchema?.fields)`, no column list), so a lookup-typed description arrives as `{ id, name }`, and the first marker click threw `Objects are not valid as a React child`. A number or a boolean description made the search box throw on the first keystroke.

One line changes behaviour, in the marker transform in `packages/plugin-map/src/ObjectMap.tsx`:

```ts
const description = recordDisplayValueAt(record, mapConfig.descriptionField);
```

`recordDisplayValueAt` is `@object-ui/core`'s shared reader in `utils/record-title`. The marker TITLE already runs it for an authored `titleField` (step 0 of `getRecordDisplayName`), and `@object-ui/plugin-detail`'s header and dedupe ladder use it too. So no new resolver is written, and the two text slots of one marker now share one rule. `MarkerData.description` was already typed as a string and now really is one, so the popup, the sheet and the search all read the same value.

| description value | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| expanded lookup `{ id: 'a1', name: 'Acme' }` | the popup throws on click; the search throws | `Acme`; the search matches `acme` |
| bare id `'a1'` (the control) | `a1` | `a1` |
| number `42` | `42`; the search throws | `42`; the search matches |
| boolean `false` | dropped by the truthiness gate; the search throws | `false` |
| expanded record with no display key `{ id: 'a1' }` | the popup throws | no description line |
| whitespace only | an empty-looking line | no description line |

No spec key changes. `descriptionField` stays out of `ListView`'s `$expand` collector: objectui#10454 excluded it on purpose, and that file is untouched.

In the same comment block, three bare line addresses that pointed into other files (`(:301)`, `(:356)`, `(:600)`) are dropped, and the symbol names beside them stay (AGENTS.md Commandment 11, repair when touched). The hunks are the import list, that comment and the description derivation. None is near the docblock paragraph that draft PR objectui#10508 edits.

## Tests (head `6134028a5`)

- **Reproduction at base `9eea12a2b`.** The pin file, run before the fix (it had 7 arms then), gave `Tests 6 failed | 1 passed (7)`. The one pass was the bare-id control. The errors were:
  - `Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {id, name})` for the popup, the reach path and the mobile sheet;
  - `TypeError: m.description?.toLowerCase is not a function` for both search arms;
  - `expected null to be 'false'` for the boolean arm.
- **Pin file** `ObjectMap.descriptionDisplay-10456.test.tsx` has 8 arms:
  - the card's expanded lookup;
  - the reach path through the map's own object fetch, which asserts that `$expand` names the lookup, then clicks;
  - the bare-id control;
  - a nameless expanded record and a blank value;
  - the mobile sheet;
  - the search on an expanded lookup;
  - number and boolean rendering;
  - the search over a number and a boolean.
- **Package suite:** `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-map/` from the repo root gave `Test Files 26 passed (26)` and `Tests 155 passed (155)`.
- **Type-check:** I built the closure first (`turbo run build --filter="@object-ui/plugin-map^..." --concurrency=2`, 13/13 tasks). Then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-map run type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exited 0. `--listFilesOnly` on the test project lists the new pin file.
- **eslint** (with and without `--no-inline-config`; `--format json` counts 2 files):
  - `ObjectMap.tsx` has the same per-rule counts as base: 13 `no-explicit-any` warnings, 0 errors.
  - The new pin carries 4 `no-explicit-any` warnings, all on the `react-map-gl` stub props. The sibling `ObjectMap.markerTitle.test.tsx` carries 7 of the same kind.
  - `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`. There is no type-aware linting, so this diff cannot move an untouched file's result.
- **Gates, all exit 0:**
  - `check:control-bytes`
  - `check:new-line-citations` (0 new)
  - `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-changeset-overwrite`
  - `check:changeset-claims`: report-only. It names one pending changeset that mentions `ObjectMap.tsx`, `6939-objectql-record-source-refinement.md`. Its paragraph is about the record-source order in `getDataConfig`, which this diff does not touch.
  - `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit` and `check:vi-mock-override-shape`
  - `check:test-path-roots`, `check:pending-changeset-literals` and `check:unreferenced-sources`
- **NOT MEASURED:** the repo-wide `pnpm test` and `pnpm lint`, which CI runs.

## Ablation (head `6134028a5`)

This used objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode, under the shared verify lock. The mutation put the raw read back: the anchor `recordDisplayValueAt(record, mapConfig.descriptionField)` became `mapConfig.descriptionField ? record[mapConfig.descriptionField] : undefined`.

- **Landed on disk:** the anchor went from 1 to 0, the replacement from 0 to 1, and the blob from `6cac44151b68` to `161639bc651e`.
- **Result, verbose reporter:** `Tests 7 failed | 1 passed (8)`. The one pass is `a bare id renders as text`, so the expanded-row pin goes red with the throw and the control stays green.
- **Restored:** the blob after restore equals the blob at HEAD (`6cac44151b68`), and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

No rebuild was needed. The pin imports `./ObjectMap` from source, and the root vitest config aliases `@object-ui/core` to `packages/core/src`.

## Acceptance notes

- **"Its display name, or its id."** The card's bare-id state (an unexpanded lookup) renders its id, as the control pins. An expanded record with none of the resolver's display keys renders no description line, because `recordDisplayValueAt` rules a bare `{ id }` payload empty. The grid's lookup cell falls back to the id instead, but that fallback lives in a private helper in `@object-ui/fields`, which this package does not depend on. Copying it here would be the third spelling the card forbids. The arm `an expanded record with no display name, and a blank value, render no description line` records this choice so it can be flipped deliberately.
- **Multi-value descriptions** (a multi-lookup or multi-select array) read as empty under the same resolver, so no line shows. Before, a string array rendered its items concatenated with no separator, and the search threw on it. Not pinned.
- **`false` and `0`.** `false` now shows as `false`. `0` now renders inside the description paragraph; before, the truthiness gate leaked a stray `0` text node beside the title.
- **Docs.** The README row for `descriptionField` ("Field shown under the title in the marker popup.") stays true, so it is unchanged.
- **Sibling finding, not fixed here:** `ObjectTimeline` has the same shape. Its own fetch expands every relation, and it passes `item[descField]` straight to the renderer as a React child. A one-shot uncommitted probe (a lookup-typed `descriptionField`, the real renderer) threw `Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {id, name})`, with `$expand: ["account"]`. The bare-id control passed. It is reported to the seat for filing.

`domain:ui` seat 1, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01BA3nKVUwKQJf8DBxrSVtNC`.
